name: Grandpacore

influenced_by: grandmillennial decorating's inherited, old-fashioned sensibility, applied to menswear instead of interiors
a broader 2020s wave of cozy-nostalgia internet aesthetics

reacts_against: contemporary slim, athletic-cut menswear norms, favoring a looser, older-fashioned silhouette worn with evident affection rather than irony.
article: Grandpacore is a 2020s internet-aesthetic tag for cozy, old-fashioned menswear — cardigans, corduroy trousers, newsboy caps, often collected secondhand — worn with the same affectionate, non-ironic nostalgia that grandmillennial decorating brings to interiors, just applied to a wardrobe instead of a living room. It sits within a broader cluster of cozy-nostalgia internet aesthetics that gained momentum through the early 2020s (cottagecore, grandmillennial, cabincore all share its basic emotional register: comfort, slowness, a preference for things that look inherited rather than newly bought). Unlike several menswear-adjacent trends that lean on irony or deliberate incongruity, grandpacore's framing — in the TikTok and Pinterest content that uses the tag — consistently presents the look as sincerely desirable rather than a joke, treating an older generation's unhurried dress sense as something worth genuinely wanting rather than merely referencing.
